title: Linear Equations & Graphs: The Perfect Straight Line

blocks.title: 1. The Core Concept: The Code of the Line
blocks.content: Every straight line you draw on a graph isn't just a random scribble�it has a mathematical 'DNA code' that perfectly describes how it moves. That code is a **Linear Equation**. It guarantees that the line is perfectly straight, with no bends or curves. If you know the equation, you can predict exactly where the line will be a million miles away without having to draw it.

blocks.title: 2. The Rules: The y = mx + c Formula
blocks.content:
The DNA of almost every straight line can be written in the famous format: **y = mx + c** (in some countries, it's y = mx + b).

� **'m' is the Gradient (Slope):** It tells you how steep the line is. A big number means a steep cliff. A positive 'm' goes uphill. A negative 'm' goes downhill.
� **'c' is the Y-Intercept:** It tells you the exact coordinate where the line crashes through the vertical y-axis. It's your 'starting point' on the graph.

blocks.title: 3. Step-by-Step: Calculating Gradient (m)
blocks.content:
To find the gradient 'm' from any two points on a line, use the **Rise over Run** method:

1. Pick two clear coordinates on the line: Point 1 (x1, y1) and Point 2 (x2, y2).
2. Calculate the **Rise**: How far UP or DOWN did you go? Subtract the y-values (y2 - y1).
3. Calculate the **Run**: How far ACROSS did you go? Subtract the x-values (x2 - x1).
4. Divide the Rise by the Run. That fraction is your gradient!

blocks.title: 4. Worked Example: Graphing the Equation
blocks.content:
Graph the line: **y = 2x - 3**

� **Step 1 (Find the start):** Look at 'c', which is -3. This means our line crosses the y-axis at -3. Put a big dot at (0, -3).
� **Step 2 (Use the slope):** Look at 'm', which is 2. This means the gradient is 2 (or 2/1). For every 1 step we Run to the right, we must Rise 2 steps up.
� **Step 3 (Find the next point):** From our starting dot at (0, -3), go RIGHT 1, and UP 2. Put a second dot at (1, -1).
� **Step 4 (Draw):** Take a ruler and draw a long straight line passing through both dots!

blocks.title: 5. Common Pitfalls
blocks.content: When calculating the gradient using (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1), the absolute most common mistake is putting the x's on top and the y's on the bottom. **Always remember: Rise (y) over Run (x).** The 'y's must be in the numerator. Also, make sure you subtract the coordinates in the exact same order for both top and bottom!
